reasoning_traces.think:
The core distinction is between cross-sectional versus longitudinal experimental designs. Normative psychology seeks comprehensive behavioral laws for a single agent, treating individual differences as noise. Individual psychology treats the agent as a random variable, seeking distributional properties across a population while controlling for stimulus context. Mathematically, this duality mirrors the covariance decomposition: Total variance = Between-group variance + Within-group variance. Failure occurs when the independence assumption breaks (e.g., learning effects, social influence), requiring hierarchical/mixed-effects models.
